# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96 (Bi-Vb Pc96)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc96
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96
**Title (English, from literature):** Not wearing a chest wrap
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 96 (*Saṁkakṣikā*) is an expiation rule for Buddhist nuns concerning the wearing of a chest wrap or bust cover (*saṁkacchika*) [Hüsken 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun who enters an inhabited village or area without wearing a bust cover commits an offense that must be confessed [Hüsken 1997]. According to its background story (*nidāna*), the regulation was laid down after a nun entered a settlement without a chest wrap; when a whirlwind blew her upper robe aside in the street, onlookers praised her waist, causing her acute embarrassment [Hüsken 1997]. The word analysis and commentary (such as the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī*) define the garment as covering the torso below the collarbone and above the navel, while the exemption formula (*anāpatti*) conforms to the standard exemptions found in monastic robe regulations [Hüsken 1997].

 An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
